item.title: Young voice takes carnival crown
item.description: YEAR 12 student Mere Mafi Sigavunau was overcome with surprise and tears of joy after being crowned Miss FMF Duavata 2026 at Subrail Park in Labasa. Ms Sigavunau, who represented Security Shield Services, received the crown during the closing of the FMF Duavata Northern Crime Prevention Carnival on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
YEAR 12 student Mere Mafi Sigavunau was overcome with surprise and tears of joy after being crowned Miss FMF Duavata 2026 at Subrail Park in Labasa.

Ms Sigavunau, who represented Security Shield Services, received the crown during the closing of the FMF Duavata Northern Crime Prevention Carnival on Saturday.

The emotional moment followed a week of advocacy, with contestants raising awareness about issues affecting communities, including drugs and substance abuse.

She thanked her fellow contestants for their support and for sharing the journey with her throughout the carnival.

“I also want to thank my fellow contestants. It has been a great pleasure to stand with you, and it has been quite a journey to share with you,” she said.

Ms Sigavunau acknowledged her parents and friends for their “endless love, support and encouragement”.

She also recognised her cousin, Josh, for supporting her throughout the competition.

She said winning the crown was a privilege and promised to carry the title with pride.

“Being crowned tonight has been a pleasure, and I promise to wear this crown with humility and dignity.”

The carnival concluded after a week of advocacy, competitions and community activities aimed at promoting crime prevention.

item.title: Accused challenges police interview
item.description: A TERTIARY student charged with the manslaughter of Jone Vuinakelo has filed an application for a voir dire challenging the admissibility of his police interview. Defence lawyer Kalisito Maisamoa, representing Aisake Lovobalavu, confirmed this to Justice Pita Bulamainaivalu in the High Court in Suva last month.
item.content:encoded:
A TERTIARY student charged with the manslaughter of Jone Vuinakelo has filed an application for a voir dire challenging the admissibility of his police interview.

Defence lawyer Kalisito Maisamoa, representing Aisake Lovobalavu, confirmed this to Justice Pita Bulamainaivalu in the High Court in Suva last month.

Mr Lovobalavu faces one count of manslaughter.

Police allege that Mr Vuinakelo, 30, was found with severe facial injuries at Nauluvatu settlement in Suva on March 15.

At the previous court sitting, Mr Maisamoa submitted that the interview was conducted immediately after a drinking session and that his client was intoxicated during prolonged police questioning.

He further alleged that parts of the interview transcript appeared to contain answers induced by police.

To support the challenge, the defence has requested disclosure of the full video recording of the interview, which has yet to be provided by the State.

The State has served the victim’s post-mortem and toxicology reports on the defence.

item.title: Market may feature annually
item.description: THE People’s Alliance party Youth Wing has committed to making its “Youth Skills Market” an annual event as it looks to create more opportunities for young entrepreneurs and connect youth with business and employment pathways. Speaking at the market, Youth Wing general secretary Kava Masilagi said the initiative was designed as a youth-focused fair and night market where young entrepreneurs and lo
item.content:encoded:
THE People’s Alliance party Youth Wing has committed to making its “Youth Skills Market” an annual event as it looks to create more opportunities for young entrepreneurs and connect youth with business and employment pathways.

Speaking at the market, Youth Wing general secretary Kava Masilagi said the initiative was designed as a youth-focused fair and night market where young entrepreneurs and local businesses could showcase their products and services.

She said the event brought together young vendors, including a 17-year-old selling homemade flower foams and slides, while also providing space for businesses to engage with potential young employees through recruitment activities.

“We’ve just really tried to make this a youth-friendly space, where youth can access other youth entrepreneurs,” Ms Masilagi said.

“And not only interact with them but also gain some encouragement.”

The market also served as a platform for employment opportunities, with companies invited to carry out recruitment drives and engage directly with young jobseekers.

Ms Masilagi said organisers deliberately brought together a mix of entrepreneurs, employers and public organisations to make the event more beneficial for young people.

“You know, there’s some youth out there who want to start up a business, but they don’t really feel that encouragement.

“So we’re hoping that seeing them in action tonight, they’d get that encouragement that they need.”

The Fijian Elections Office was also among the organisations participating, with the aim of making information and services more accessible in a setting designed specifically to attract young people.

Ms Masilagi said organisers hope the Youth Skills Market will continue to grow as an annual event, providing a regular platform for youth entrepreneurship, networking and employment opportunities.

item.title: Kamikamica leaves Cabinet decision to Prime Minister after acquittal
item.description: Former Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica says it is entirely up to Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka whether he returns to Cabinet following his acquittal by the Suva Magistrates Court today. Speaking to the media outside court after the magistrate ruled he had no case to answer, Kamikamica said he remained committed to serving Fiji in whatever capacity he was asked.
item.content:encoded:
Former Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica says it is entirely up to Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka whether he returns to Cabinet following his acquittal by the Suva Magistrates Court today.

Speaking to the media outside court after the magistrate ruled he had no case to answer, Kamikamica said he remained committed to serving Fiji in whatever capacity he was asked.

“As far as I’m concerned, that’s up to the Honourable Prime Minister. It’s got nothing to do with me,” he said when asked whether he would seek the return of his ministerial portfolio.

Kamikamica said he had stepped aside when the charges were filed and was now focused on his current role as Chair of the Public Accounts Committee.

“I did what I had to do when the charges came up. So I’m quite happy at the moment doing the Public Accounts chairmanship work. We are doing a lot of good things there.”

He said his priority had always been serving the country rather than holding office.

“As you know, I joined this role to serve our country, and whatever the Honourable Prime Minister has in store, I will accept that with grace and humility.”

Kamikamica also expressed relief at the outcome of the court proceedings, saying he believed justice had prevailed.

“Right now, I’m just so relieved that justice was served today.”

He said he hoped the ruling would strengthen public confidence and allow the country to focus on the future.

“Hopefully, it puts a lot of confidence in some of the things that people are saying and people are doing, and we can continue to move forward as a country. There’s a lot to do.”

item.title: Kamikamica acquitted after court finds no case to answer
item.description: Former Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica has been acquitted after the Suva Magistrates Court ruled that he has no case to answer on criminal charges brought against him by the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption (FICAC). Magistrate Charles Ratakele delivered the ruling at the Suva Magistrates Court this afternoon, dismissing the case after finding there was insufficient evidence to
item.content:encoded:
Former Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica has been acquitted after the Suva Magistrates Court ruled that he has no case to answer on criminal charges brought against him by the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption (FICAC).

Magistrate Charles Ratakele delivered the ruling at the Suva Magistrates Court this afternoon, dismissing the case after finding there was insufficient evidence to require Kamikamica to enter a defence.

Kamikamica had been charged with one count of perjury, alleging that he falsely stated under oath during the 2024 Commission of Inquiry into the appointment of former FICAC Commissioner Barbara Malimali that he had no knowledge of her appointment before it was publicly announced on September 5, 2024.

In the alternative, he faced one count of providing false information to a public servant based on the same alleged statement made to the Commission of Inquiry.

Last week, defence lawyer Wylie Clarke applied for the charges to be dismissed after the prosecution closed its case, arguing there was insufficient evidence to establish the essential elements of either offence.

The prosecution, led by Senior Prosecutors Josann Pene and Setefano Komaibaba, had called two witnesses during the trial—lawyer Janet Mason and Government backbencher Kalaveti Ravu.

Following today’s ruling that there was no case to answer, Kamikamica was acquitted of both charges, bringing the proceedings to an end.

item.title: Strong wind alert in force for parts of Fiji
item.description: The Fiji Meteorological Service has issued a Strong Wind Alert for several parts of the country, warning residents and mariners to take precautions as strong winds and hazardous sea conditions affect the group. The alert is now in force for the land areas of Yasawa, the coastal areas of Rakiraki and Sigatoka, the Lau and Lomaiviti groups, Taveuni and nearby smaller islands, Kadavu and nearby small
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Meteorological Service has issued a Strong Wind Alert for several parts of the country, warning residents and mariners to take precautions as strong winds and hazardous sea conditions affect the group.

The alert is now in force for the land areas of Yasawa, the coastal areas of Rakiraki and Sigatoka, the Lau and Lomaiviti groups, Taveuni and nearby smaller islands, Kadavu and nearby smaller islands, Southern Bua and Udu Point. It also applies to all Fiji waters.

The weather office is urging people in the affected areas to stay informed, secure loose items around their homes and properties, and monitor the latest weather updates.

Mariners, particularly those operating small boats and vessels, have been warned that strong winds will create rough and hazardous sea conditions.

The Fiji Meteorological Service is advising against unnecessary travel at sea where conditions are unsafe and has urged boat owners to ensure vessels and equipment are properly secured.

Those already at sea are encouraged to closely monitor weather conditions and follow advice issued by the relevant authorities.

The weather office is reminding the public to exercise caution and avoid putting themselves or others at unnecessary risk while the strong wind conditions persist.

item.title: 796 coronary angiograms performed at Lautoka Hospital Cath Lab
item.description: The Cath Lab at Lautoka Hospital has performed 796 coronary angiograms since commencing the service in May 2025, providing hundreds of Fijians with access to advanced cardiac diagnostic care closer to home. In a statement, Aspen Medical said a coronary angiogram is the gold-standard imaging procedure used to diagnose coronary artery disease by giving cardiologists a detailed view of the heart’s bl
item.content:encoded:
The Cath Lab at Lautoka Hospital has performed 796 coronary angiograms since commencing the service in May 2025, providing hundreds of Fijians with access to advanced cardiac diagnostic care closer to home.

In a statement, Aspen Medical said a coronary angiogram is the gold-standard imaging procedure used to diagnose coronary artery disease by giving cardiologists a detailed view of the heart’s blood vessels.

The procedure enables doctors to detect blockages, assess heart health and determine the most appropriate treatment at an early stage.

Aspen Medical said the service has allowed many patients to receive accurate and timely diagnoses without the need to travel overseas.

The healthcare provider said every early diagnosis creates an opportunity for earlier treatment, improved health outcomes and greater peace of mind for patients and their families.

Aspen Medical said expanding access to world-class cardiac diagnostic services at Lautoka Hospital is helping transform heart care across Fiji, one patient at a time.

item.title: AI rapidly shifts to operational hazard
item.description: ARTIFICIAL intelligence is rapidly shifting from a technical novelty into an immediate operational hazard, rapidly upskilling threat actors and forcing organisations to overhaul their approach to risk management. National Risk Solution director Chris Graham made these comments while speaking at the Pacific Fiber Conference 2026 in Nadi, saying brokers and underwriters across global hubs from Londo
item.content:encoded:
ARTIFICIAL intelligence is rapidly shifting from a technical novelty into an immediate operational hazard, rapidly upskilling threat actors and forcing organisations to overhaul their approach to risk management.

National Risk Solution director Chris Graham made these comments while speaking at the Pacific Fiber Conference 2026 in Nadi, saying brokers and underwriters across global hubs from London to Singapore had reported that cyber exposures now reached into hundreds of millions of dollars.

The core issue, experts warn, is that tools once locked behind months of specialist dark web collaboration are now broadly accessible.

Mr Graham said AI was effectively arming unsophisticated criminals overnight, accelerating deceptive tactics like targeted phishing and automated fraud.

At the same time, he said companies were eagerly embedding AI into internal workflows to capture efficiency gains.

Yet, he added that rapid adoption had created dangerous blind spots around unapproved employee software, data transfers, and rogue automated agents.

“Risk management cannot remain a once-a-year exercise, cyber risk is now a business loss issue, not only a technical incident,” Mr Graham said.

“It can become downtime, lost money, legal cost, reputational damage, and recovery expense,” he said.

While human error and everyday scams remained frequent drivers of claims, Mr Graham said high-severity events like ransomware continued to dominate organisational losses.

Modern insurance covers must now serve as active resilience tools funding threat monitoring, forensics, and crisis response rather than acting as passive payout policies.

To withstand evolving threats, Mr Graham proposed that leaders must regularly test internal controls, establish clear accountability for AI failures, and present verifiable risk management practices directly to underwriters before severe market losses occur.
